Hi Marissa,

We saw a sustained slowdown across our inference calls between ~10:45–11:20 UTC this morning. Latency spiked from our usual 120–250ms to ~1.8s and a ~3% error rate for tokenization failures. This impacted two production routes and caused timed-out requests in our payments validation flow.

Can you share an initial RCA and concrete next steps for verification and remediation? Compliance needs a written summary by EOD tomorrow. We appreciate the fast response — this is blocking a scheduled go-live for our Q2 feature.

Thanks,
Alejandra Ruiz
Head of Platform Engineering
Starbridge Payments

Subject: Fwd: Starbridge slowdown — quick sync and action owners

Team — forwarding the customer note. Key asks: one-page RCA + timeline within 24h, full RCA with logs/controls in 72h, verification plan and evidence for compliance.

Quick proposed diagnostic summary (please confirm):
- Symptom: tokenization failures + elevated latency on two production routes, spike 10:45–11:20 UTC.
- Probable immediate cause: concurrent rolling kernel switch on two GPU pools handling Starbridge traffic + an edge cache miss storm that amplified p99 latency.
- Impact: elevated latency (250ms -> 1.8s), ~3% tokenization errors, intermittent 504s for long-running calls.

Action owners (proposed):
- Karthik: validate kernel switch logs, confirm whether the rolling change overlapped with Starbridge dedicated pool (JIRA-OPS-1429).
- Olga: assemble tokenization failure traces, token counts, and prefix/KV cache hit/miss rates for the window.
- Hannah: coordinate the customer bridge, compliance timeline, and delivery of the one-page summary.
- Me: customer-facing communications and executive summary.

Please reply with short confirmations and any additional follow-ups by +30 minutes. We need artifacts for the 24h note.

—Marissa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Starbridge slowdown — quick sync and action owners

Confirming. Initial findings attached (impact_timeline_20270502.csv).

Short technical summary for the 24h customer note:
- Root cause: a queued kernel rollout on our inference runtime coincided with a high-cardinality prefix cache eviction pattern for Starbridge routes. During the rollout, a small percentage of hosts served models with a kernel variant that had a fallback path increasing tokenization latency under heavy prefix miss rates.
- Contributing factor: autoscaling burst behavior caused transient rebalancing across hosts, increasing cache miss amplification.
- Immediate mitigations already executed: rolled back the kernel rollout on affected hosts (completed 11:40 UTC), pinned Starbridge routes to a stable model variant, and increased short-term cache retention for prefixes to reduce thrash.

Next actions (owners & ETA):
- Full log capture & forensics (Olga) — ETA 24h.
- Controlled re-run test on a mirror pool to validate fixes — ETA 48h (JIRA-OPS-1429).
- Runtime guard: add a pre-commit check to prevent kernel rollouts during high-traffic windows for pinned customer pools — ETA 2 weeks.

Karthik
Lead, Runtime Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@starbridge.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Starbridge — Incident summary and corrective actions (initial RCA)

Alejandra — thank you again for the bridge today. Attached is a brief RCA and an impact timeline CSV for your compliance team. Below is a concise customer-facing summary and the verification plan.

Executive summary:
- Window: 2027-05-02 10:45–11:20 UTC
- Impact: increased p99 latency (typical 120–250ms -> observed 1.8s), tokenization-related error rate ~3%, and intermittent 504s on two production routes used by your payments validation flow.
- Root cause: an in-progress kernel rollout on a subset of inference hosts overlapped with an unusually high number of prefix cache misses for Starbridge traffic. The kernel variant on a minority of hosts triggered a slower tokenization fallback under those miss conditions.

Actions taken (completed):
1) Immediate rollback of the kernel rollout on affected hosts — completed 11:40 UTC.
2) Pinned Starbridge routes to the stable model variant to avoid future kernel-variant exposure.
3) Increased short-term prefix cache retention for your routes to reduce miss amplification.

Planned near-term actions (ETA / owner):
- Forensics package (Olga) — full traces, histograms, and log slices for 10:30–11:30 UTC (ETA 24h).
- Mirror-run verification on a shadow pool to confirm no regression after re-deployment (Karthik) — ETA 48h.
- Policy change: temporary runtime guard to block kernel rollouts affecting pinned pools during customer business hours (Product + Runtime) — ETA 2 weeks.

Verification plan for compliance:
- Deliverables: one-page RCA PDF, impact_timeline CSV, and forensic logs in Drive (link below).
- Validation window: Redwood will run a controlled replay against a mirror pool and share metrics (latency histograms, KV cache hit rates, tokenization error counts).
- Acceptance criteria: p99 latency returns to baseline (<=300ms) and tokenization errors <0.1% in the replay run.

Links & artifacts:
- Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-starbridge-rca
- Ticket: JIRA-OPS-1429
- Attachments: starbridge_rca_20270502.pdf, impact_timeline_20270502.csv

We take this seriously and will provide the full forensic packet within the 72-hour window. Please let me know if you want an executive note tailored for your compliance officers.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
